note: Dated events for this scenario, drawn only from mechanics the engine already has. Dates are the year and the week of that year. Magnitudes follow docs/rules/CONTENT-PACING.md. Titles and summaries are fictional framing with no real company or person names.

events.title: A browser company goes public
events.summary: A start-up that makes web browsers lists on the exchange and its shares more than double on the first day. Everyone wants to be online.

events.title: A new desktop operating system launches
events.summary: A new version of the dominant desktop operating system ships with built in networking. Software and hardware makers rush to match it.

events.title: A currency crisis abroad
events.summary: Currencies in Asia fall sharply. Overseas buyers cancel orders and lenders at home get cautious.

events.title: The year 2000 repair rush
events.summary: Companies rush to fix old software before the calendar rolls over. Consultancies and services firms cannot hire fast enough.

events.title: The year 2000 spending hangover
events.summary: The calendar rolled over without disaster. Firms stop spending on fixes and cancel the projects that followed.

events.title: The dot-com bust
events.summary: Internet share prices crash and funding for start-ups dries up. Chip prices fall and venture capital becomes scarce.

events.title: The economy slips into recession
events.summary: Layoffs spread beyond technology. The central bank cuts rates to cushion the fall.

events.title: Too many chip plants
events.summary: The boom years left the world with more chip capacity than it needs. Prices for chips keep falling.

events.title: Technology spending recovers
events.summary: Firms replace old equipment and a new wave of web services appears. Demand for technology goods and services picks up.
